description: Bare technical call: after any computed plan wipe, leaves the repo at the surviving base plus everything the accepted plan-changing call introduced. No craft law, no battery.

text: TASK: the accepted plan computed a wipe boundary, and git has rewound
the workspace to it. The driver then attempted to apply exactly the
accepted change range named below onto that base. This call runs for EVERY
computed wipe boundary, including deletion, forbidden insertion, and
forbidden reorder, whether the preliminary apply was clean, conflicted,
Leave the repo at that base PLUS everything the accepted call introduced —
documents and code alike, the skeleton included: the accepted range
wins. The only work that stays undone is the wiped/requeued slices' — they will
be re-implemented on this base. Leave no conflict markers behind.

variables.name: wipe_reason
variables.description: Why the plan computed a wipe boundary and which slices were unwound/requeued.

variables.name: wipe_boundary
variables.description: Commit restored before the accepted change range is re-landed; never the source-range start.

variables.name: source_base_role
variables.description: pre_session_commit for Brainstorming; pre_call_commit for a direct agent call

variables.name: source_base_revision
variables.description: Commit captured before the accepted plan-changing call; source-range start and never the wipe boundary by implication.

variables.name: accepted_revision
variables.description: Source-range end: the common ready commit for Brainstorming, or the driver's commit of an accepted direct-call result.

variables.name: apply_outcome
variables.description: clean, conflicted, rejected, partial, or empty

variables.name: apply_diagnostics
variables.description: Git diagnostics plus the resulting index/work-tree state and affected paths; use 'none' only for a genuinely clean or empty apply.

questions.status: bare technical kind — no battery by design (decision 57)
